newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Investment doubles index funds - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Investment doubles index funds - WSJ.

text.p: The new chief of Fidelty Investment's retail unit is doubling the number of index funds sold by the company to six, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

The paper also reported that Fidelity is planning to announce a joint venture with a Wall Street securities firm to sell initial public offerings and that the firm will shut its foreign exchange trading desk.

The Journal said new chief Paul Hondros's moves are an effort to reposition Fidelity as a more conservative, low-cost company. Raising the number of its index funds is also a shot at Vanguard Group, whose index funds have been beating Fidelity in gathering new assets, the newspaper said.

The effort to increase Fidelity's index funds is the latest indication that the fund industry might be headed towards greater recognition that many investors want to ride the market up, rather than rely on a fund manager's picks for greater returns, the Journal said.
Hondros, who joined Fidelity's retail unit in September, denied to the Journal that he plans to lay off employees.
